description: Table 1, a two-column table rendered as an image, titled by its caption "Thermodynamic parameter expressions and values (T is temperature, K)". The left column is headed "Thermodynamic parameters" and the right column "Expressions/Values". It lists eight rows of free-energy differences for the γ→ε (fcc→hcp) transformation used to estimate stacking fault energy: ΔG_Fe^(γ→ε) = −1828.4 + 4.686T; ΔG_Mn^(γ→ε) = 3970–1.667T; ΔG_Al^(γ→ε) = 5481.04–1.7991T; ΔG_C^(γ→ε) = −22.166; ΔG_FeMn^(γ→ε) = −9135.5 + 15.2821X_Mn; ΔG_FeAl^(γ→ε) = 3326.280; ΔG_FeC^(γ→ε) = 42.500; and ΔG_FeMnAl/C^(γ→ε) = 1246(1-e^−24.29X_C)/X_C − 17175X_Mn. All entries are pure numbers or linear/empirical expressions in temperature T and mole fractions X_Mn and X_C; no curves, images or scale bars are present. This is a lookup/reference table supplying the input parameters for the SFE equation; the citing text states these values feed equation (4) and that the SFE of the experimental Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si steel is estimated at 32, 40 and 61 mJ/m² for −196 °C, −77 °C and RT respectively.
measured_quantities: γ→ε free-energy difference ΔG (J/mol, expressed in T and X)

observations.observation: The table has two columns headed 'Thermodynamic parameters' and 'Expressions/Values', listing eight γ→ε free-energy difference terms.
ΔG_FeAl^(γ→ε) is given as 3326.280 and ΔG_FeC^(γ→ε) as 42.500.
The caption states that T is temperature in K.
The citing text states that these thermodynamic expressions and required parameters are for equation (4).
The citing text states the SFE of the experimental steel at −196 °C, −77 °C and RT is estimated to be 32, 40 and 61 mJ/m² respectively; these values are not printed in the table.

The citing text defines ΔG_i^(γ→ε) as the free-energy difference between the fcc and hcp structures of a given alloying element and ΔG_ij^(γ→ε) as the interaction-energy difference of two alloying elements.

subfigures.description: A two-column table: left column 'Thermodynamic parameters' lists eight free-energy terms ΔG_i^(γ→ε) for Fe, Mn, Al, C, FeMn, FeAl, FeC and FeMnAl/C; right column 'Expressions/Values' gives the corresponding numeric constants or expressions in T, X_Mn and X_C.
